reading: The input is the left half of an open outline. Mirror it about the vertical line just right of its rightmost column to close the shape, then output only the shape's interior filled with the shape colour (the outline itself is erased).
verb: complete symmetric outline and fill interior

slots.axis: vertical line just right of the object's rightmost column
slots.fill: interior of the completed outline, in the object's colour
slots.erase: the outline cells (input and mirrored) become background

why: on every pair the output's filled cells are exactly the cells strictly inside the outline completed by mirroring

reading: A 2-coloured arm is attached to a 5 pivot. The arm turns 90 degrees clockwise about the pivot (same length, colour 2), and the arm's old cells become 3.

slots.arm: the straight run of 2s touching the pivot

why: on every pair the new 2 run has the arm's length and points 90 degrees clockwise from the old direction; the old run is all 3

reading: Each hollow square of 5 has its hole filled with a colour set by the hole size: 1x1 hole -> 6, 2x2 -> 7, 3x3 -> 8.
why: every interior cell is filled with the size-keyed colour; nothing outside the holes changes

reading: The 1-row input with one 2 becomes a WxW square: a V of 2s runs diagonally down-left and down-right from the 2 to the side borders, and inside the V, down-right diagonals of 1 are drawn every 4 cells parallel to the right arm.

slots.size: output is W x W, W = input width
slots.arms: two diagonals of 2 from the apex to the left and right borders
slots.hatch: down-right diagonals of 1 at offsets 4, 8, ... below the right arm, kept only below the left arm

why: on every pair, 2s lie on |x-c| = y for y <= c, and 1s lie on cells with y-x+c a positive multiple of 4 and y > c-x

reading: Every full row and every full column made only of 0s is painted 2.

new_rows.name: zline
new_rows.datalog:
z(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C = 0.
nzrow(Y) :- px(Y, X, C), !z(Y, X).
nzcol(X) :- px(Y, X, C), !z(Y, X).
zline(Y, X) :- z(Y, X), !nzrow(Y).
zline(Y, X) :- z(Y, X), !nzcol(X).

why: the cells that change are exactly the cells of all-0 rows and columns, all to colour 2

reading: The 3x3 input is scaled into a 3x3 grid of blocks: a block holds a copy of the input where the input cell has the input's most common colour; other blocks are empty.
why: each output block is the input exactly when the matching input cell is the most common (background) colour, else all 0
invariants: the unit is the whole input unchanged

reading: Background-coloured columns split the grid into panels, each with one pattern colour. In each panel the background cells take the pattern colour of the next panel to the right, the last panel taking the first panel's colour; the separator columns stay.

slots.panels: vertical stripes cut by full columns of the background colour
slots.subject: background cells inside each panel
slots.colour: the non-background colour of the next panel (cyclic, last -> first)

why: every background cell of panel i becomes the colour of panel i+1 mod n; pattern cells and separator columns are unchanged

reading: Each hollow square has 1-bars on the grid border in line with it. The square is copied edge to edge (period = its size) from itself toward each such bar until the border; the bars are covered.

slots.subject: each hollow square object (not colour 1)
slots.direction: toward each 1-bar on the border that shares the square's rows or columns

why: on every pair the output equals the squares plus abutting copies running from each square to every border bar aligned with it
invariants: squares with no bar stay single

reading: Some rectangles have a one-cell-wide tail. Each such rectangle moves in the tail's direction by the tail's length and the tail disappears; rectangles it was covering are shown complete, and the moved rectangle covers anything at its new place.

slots.subject: each solid rectangle with a thin protruding line
slots.occlusion: partly hidden rectangles are restored to full rectangles; moved rectangle drawn on top

why: each tailed rectangle keeps its shape and ends shifted by tail length along the tail; tailless rectangles keep place (completed where uncovered)

reading: Tile the input 3x3. Then every row containing a coloured cell is filled with 1 (except the coloured cells), and each coloured cell gets a 3 at its up-left and down-right diagonal neighbours.

slots.line: rows holding a coloured cell: background becomes 1
slots.marks: 3 at (y-1,x-1) and (y+1,x+1) of every coloured cell in the tiled grid, if in bounds

why: on every pair the output equals the 3x3 tiling with 1-rows through coloured cells and 3s on their main-diagonal neighbours
